findings.text: `parse_claude` (and `parse_codex` at :233, `launches` at :45) re-implements the per-stream token measurement and stream discovery the repository already owns in `reckon/crew/metering.py`: `measure_stream_tokens` at :73, `_claude_usage` at :161, `_codex_usage` at :207 and `run_streams` at :319. The duplicate carries the same Claude dedupe-by-message-id rule and the same peak-context figure (`maximum_request_input_tokens`). It duplicates rather than extends or wraps that owner, so a correction to the owner's reading will not reach this record and the two can drift silently.

`launches()` returns only `stream.jsonl` and `resume-*.jsonl`, dropping `lane-change-*.jsonl`; `reckon/crew/metering.py:319` `run_streams` includes lane-change streams specifically because a lane change keeps the run id and its spend would otherwise be silently lost. None of this wave's five runs carries a lane-change stream, so no figure in the record moves, but the next wave's run that changes lane would report a cumulative input missing that lane's work.

The departures paragraph ('Two sections departed from the draw: ...') and the arm-membership paragraph at :839 are hardcoded prose in `render()`, while the record's own method section states the record is 'generated, not transcribed'. A second wave regenerates the tables from data but renders these literals unchanged, so prose describing a population of five would sit beside tables describing a different one.
